segments.text: What if you could literally see what bad design does to your brain?
We used Meta's new brain model to simulate fMRI scans for different UI experiences.
Clean UI versus cluttered UI. Same task, completely different brain activation. The cluttered version makes your frontal cortex work overtime.
But here's the wild part. Dark checkout patterns actually flip your brain's reward signal positive. Pre-checked add-ons and exclusive deals hijack your reward circuit even while manipulating you.
That's the neural mechanism dark patterns exploit. Your brain literally rewards you for being tricked.
Flow-breaking UI doubles your cognitive load. Constant interruptions, slow autocomplete — your brain fights to stay focused. High engagement, but it's struggle, not flow.
And cryptic errors? They collapse your brain's spatial clarity. You literally lose your sense of where you are in the interface.
We derived eight brain signals — cognitive load, frustration, flow, trust — that could power autonomous UI design.
Bad UX doesn't just annoy you. It measurably disrupts your brain. Good design is literally brain-friendly design.
